newsitem.title: USA: Motorola expands suit against Qualcomm.
newsitem.headline: Motorola expands suit against Qualcomm.

text.p: Motorola Inc said it filed a new patent infringement lawsuit against Qualcomm Inc expanding current lawsuits by including patent infringement of certain cellular phone products and certain integrated circuits.

The suit, filed late yesterday in Federal District Court in San Diego, seeks to have Qualcomm permanently enjoined from further infringement of these patents and seeks damages for Qualcomm's past infringement.

"This new lawsuit is a result of Motorola's on-going effort to examine all of Qualcomm's recent conduct and bring appropriate new infringement claims before the court," said Suzette Steiger, corporate vice president and assistant general manager of Motorola's Pan American cellular subsciber group.

"Motorola is not willing to allow Qualcomm to misuse Motorola's intellectual property while at the same time demanding that Motorola pay high royalties to properly use Qualcomm's intellectual property," she said in a statement.

Steiger said that although Motorola and Qualcomm signed cross-license agreements in 1990 that grant Qualcomm a royalty-bearing license to use some of Motorola's patents, the patents that are the subject of this new lawsuit are not licensed to Qualcomm.

"Qualcomm seeks to ignore the limits of our agreements by claiming the right to use any Motorola patents that it wishes. Motorola will not stand by while Qualcomm continues to disregard to Motorola's rights," said Steiger.
In March, Motorola filed a patent infringement suit against Qualcomm over Qualcomm's Q-phone.
